Benefiting from solid solution strengthening, second-phase strengthening, and the crack-buffering effects of body-centered cubic (BCC) phase, the proposed alloys achieved high HT strength while maintaining appreciable RT plasticity.

The significant elastic interaction between the local stress fields of component atoms and dislocations in BCC phase leads to more pronounced solid solution strengthening.
For C0.5 alloy, the dislocation aggregation in the primary bulk BCC phase and the dislocation annihilation resulting from dynamic recovery near the boundary reach a balance.
In C1.3 alloy, the inferior dislocation accumulating ability of the primary HCP-M2C phase promotes more pronounced dynamic recovery and dynamic recrystallization, resulting in HT softening.
